title: Boards of abstract names
claim: Names are a countably infinite set with no letters; a state gives each unordered pair of names a neighbour distinction and each name a value; a uniform law applies its templates to every tuple alike. Proved: (T1) every finitary law that allows a state allows one with constant adjacency and values, or with identity distinctions all names one place (Ramsey), so a finitary law can bound the degree but never force a neighbour and forces no finite board other than one place; (T2) every countable simple 2k-regular graph splits into k fixed-point-free permutations, so a degree supplied by existence clauses carries a labelling, which no clause can read; (T3) a count law allows every countable cover and disjoint union of its boards, hence a tree whenever it allows a cycle, while a finitary clause reading a walk of distinct names can exclude the tree; (T4) no law of bounded degree forces a connected infinite board (compactness), and a named square with coordinates mod 3 and an aperiodic Wang set has exactly the disjoint unions of tiled planes as boards; (T5) in a count law of degree d >= 1, two edges with one pair of values exchange partners (a four-distinction change that changes the board when the edge lies on a cycle of a finite component) and names can be exchanged, so at a state of infinitely many copies of a two-valued board every distinction is flipped by a finite change and the source-aware condition excludes nothing. Read before publication by an independent referee; checks passed.
failure_conditions: A finitary law with an allowed state and no state of constant adjacency and values (against T1).
A countable 2k-regular simple graph with no decomposition into k oriented 2-factors (against T2).
A count law with a board containing a cycle and no tree board (against T3, and A54 overturned).
A first-order law all of whose boards are connected while one has a component of infinite diameter (against T4).
A count-law state in which the switch or the swap breaks the law (against T5).
foundation_claim_scope: Boards made of neighbour distinctions on a countable set of names with no letters; uniform laws over finite alphabets, finitary or with existence clauses. Neighbour distinctions are distinctions of the law, never contact by themselves (A51).

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the coordinator's go-ahead on 2026-11-10; read before publication by an independent referee (a fresh Claude agent given only the proof).

validation.novelty: Every ingredient classical (Ramsey, Petersen, Hall and Mendelsohn-Dulmage, compactness, covering graphs, aperiodic Wang tiles; the switch is the graph-theoretic 2-switch); each statement a short consequence, folklore risk high. The reading for the board line is this epic's.
